KPV GmbHBubos Physiotherapie

01Medium-sized companyPayroll department of a large car wash chain · Document management

Tried for years. Done in one.

The head of payroll had been trying to go digital for years – it never worked. Together we managed it within a year: everything that used to be processed, passed back and forth and filed on paper is now digital.

  • Processes examined closely and improved.
  • A professional document management system introduced.
  • No more paper is produced internally; paper from outside has been reduced and has largely disappeared.
  • Re-sorting and big filing sessions at the end of the year are a thing of the past.
  • The team contributes its own ideas and now uses AI too.

A boss who gives you free rein helps enormously.

02Medium-sized companyExcel spreadsheet replaced · Web application

92 columns of Excel. Now an app.

Door orders used to be costed in an Excel spreadsheet with 92 columns. Today a tailor-made application does the job – from site measurements to the data sheet.

  • The project manager takes a Surface PC to the building site and records the measurements directly on the plan.
  • Later, back at the office, he completes the specifications at his leisure.
  • He shares the data sheets with the architect for approval.

Goodbye, column 92.

03Medium-sized companyFacility management for business and pharmaceutical parks · SharePoint introduction

First one department. Then the whole company.

One department wanted to move away from folders and drives on the file server – to SharePoint.

  • Training came first, so that everyone understood the advantages and limits of SharePoint.
  • Then we built the new structure together – with an eye on what SharePoint can do beyond a drive – and introduced it with ground rules.
  • That won people over: today the whole company keeps its documents in SharePoint, with its own sites, libraries and ground rules for each department.
  • The result: more transparency, less version chaos, information changed and shared faster.

Less version chaos.

04Small businessCustomer service at a joinery · Web application

Material requested. Ordered. Checked.

For a joinery’s customer service jobs we built a tailor-made app: from the request for material to the completed job.

  • Service technicians report the material they need – on site or at the office.
  • The office orders centrally, including several jobs in one order.
  • The app matches order confirmations and delivery notes against the orders. The AI pre-fills, a person checks.
  • Once the material has arrived, the technician sees it on the job and can complete it.

No more chasing.

05Small businessMetalworking business in the Lüneburg Heath · Processes, Trello, ERP introduction

Processes first. Then the software.

A metalworking business wanted to work more digitally and efficiently. Before, there was a lot of paper and a lot of uncertainty in the processes.

  • Core processes mapped and optimised.
  • Temporarily set up in Trello to test whether they were right – that alone brought much more transparency to projects and customer orders.
  • In parallel, we gathered the requirements for new ERP software, looked for suppliers, tested the favourite and supported the introduction.
  • Along the way, we redesigned the digital filing and introduced the Kanban method.

Next project: the warehouse.

06Small businessIndustry software extended · Browser extension

The industry software can do more now.

Proven industry software for trade businesses – it just lacked one complex calculation. Instead of switching software, we extended it.

  • An assistant plugs straight into the invoice: enter dimensions, compartments and shelves, and the area, fittings and price are worked out.
  • The result lands in the invoice as a finished line item.
  • Built as a browser extension. Possible because the software – Mein Handwerker (mein-handwerker-app.de) – runs in the browser and has a programming interface.

Extend instead of switching.

07Small businessSole trader with many properties · One-to-one coaching

The whole business. Digital.

A businesswoman wanted to reinvent herself and her business. Before, there was endless paper in several offices; almost everything with tenants and the property managers was done on paper.

  • New devices bought, switch from Windows to Apple.
  • Software installed, accounts set up, workflows rebuilt.
  • Trained in one-to-one coaching sessions – the know-how is now hers.
  • Working with the property managers, tenants and tax adviser is now entirely digital.

All data. Anytime. Anywhere.

08Small businessShared home for people with disabilities · Google Sheets

Every quarter of an hour recorded. The billing writes itself.

The carers in a shared home for people with disabilities record their activities in fine detail throughout the day – for individual residents or for groups.

  • The spreadsheet spots clashes and inconsistencies by itself.
  • At the end of the month, the service records for the funding bodies are produced.
  • Deliberately built as a Google Sheets application: at the start the processes weren’t clear yet, and a lot of flexibility was needed.

Not every solution has to be an app.

09Small businessTraining academy for tradespeople · Workshops and training

Tired? Far from it.

An academy worked in a very traditional, paper-heavy way. A new manager brought new energy to question how things were done.

  • Joint workshops uncovered a lot of potential: make better use of existing software, drop many small unnecessary steps.
  • Then training in Microsoft 365, which is being introduced right now.
  • The surprise: the staff had lots of ideas of their own – even sceptics were won over.

The ideas were there all along.

10CorporationLarge company in southern Germany · Clear-outs, training, workshops

Tonnes less paper.

Over several years we worked with almost all the office departments of a very large company – from purchasing and sales to marketing and research and development. Everyone wanted to work digitally and cut out outdated processes.

  • It started with big clear-outs – with far more momentum than expected. In the end, everyone parted with much more than they had intended.
  • Clearing up showed how much waste there is in everyday work. Collected along the way: ideas for simplifying and going digital.
  • Lots of cupboards were freed up. The move into new, modern offices was made with light luggage.
  • Then came training on the tools and workshops on Microsoft 365 and time management – so that work carries on well organised.

Let go of more than planned.

Your process could be the next case.
